questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to experience the American academic culture, which involves a lot of in-class participation and engagement

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The application process was a bit confusing and chaotic. I thought KU would assist in the application process. However, I did it all alone. I would recommend asking questions to the exchange program manager at the destination university as they helped me tremendously

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Once I arrived, it was very easy to get help if I needed any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Quadruple dorm rooms, double rooms, single rooms, apartment styles, and suites.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: It depends on your housing situation. All dorm rooms meaning quadruple, double, and single, demand a BU campus dining hall meal plan. There was a broad selection to choose from.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You are not guaranteed any room. As an exchange student, you are granted a room last. Thus, the chances of getting a suite or apartment style are slim. I got a quadruple room, and I was very dissatisfied. So, I contacted the housing services and persistently asked for a single room. After a week, I got one.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would only recommend on-campus housing if you like having people around you at all times. Also, remember that American students are generally younger, so expect most on-campus students to be around 18 years old. That was my experience.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy to register for classes. However, American students have first priority meaning a lot of classes are full by the time you, as an exchange student, can enroll in classes. So, I recommend having 2-3 backup classes if the ones you want are full.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I had to fill out a form and send a copy to the program manager. I got an immediate response, which was nice, so I didn't have to wait to know if I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The program coordinator was always available and very helpful. In general, the service level at BU was incredible.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted except for one. All in all, I was satisfied.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask questions to BU if you have any. They are very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I learned a lot. I am very happy that I decided to study at BU. The professors were very engaging, which made it all much more interesting. The classes were shorter than at KU, and there was way more in-class participation and tests/quizzes/exams. Be prepared for a vastly different academic system and structure.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the classes interesting and easy to follow. The number of readings was similar to KU. However, there were more quizzes, tests, and exams. After the first weeks, I found that I became pretty desensitized to them, so it wasn't stressful.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes are shorter, but there is more participation, as participation is considered in your grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "Understanding Media", "Public Practices of Public Relations", and "General Psychology".

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. Especially Understanding Media! Very interesting with many current examples.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I lived on campus, so whenever I wanted something, like tea, I had to buy one. So, I definitely spend a lot of money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The laundry rooms on campus are not free. Expect to pay for everything :D

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs to join. Some are more active than others. I joined two, but they didn't host any events for the semester I was there, which was a bit annoying.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a large fitness center with every possible fitness equipment. Very nice facilities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think that depends on your personal preferences.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I visited the different areas in Massachusetts. I also went to New York, which is always fun.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it fairly easy. People are very open and inclusive.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I don't think you will have any trouble. It was very easy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness and curiosity.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be financially prepared 
2. Really consider your living situation. On campus means a LOT of young students. 
3. You can always earn extra credit, but try to balance academics with social activities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not anything that I haven't covered.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My academic experience and the friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Tolerating people's really bad manners in the dining hall.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
